name: Willandra Lakes Region
description: In the semi-arid Far West of New South Wales, the Willandra Lakes Region covers 2,400 square kilometres of dry lake beds and wind-sculpted sand dunes. The lakes filled and emptied during the Ice Age, and they left behind giant marsupial fossils and traces of human life 45,000 to 60,000 years old. They include the world's oldest known cremation, in the Mungo National Park area.
